title: Emilia-Romagna's Metano Prices Are Outrunning the Rest of Italy
dek: A quiet day at the pump masks a ten-week trend: natural gas is climbing nearly four points faster here than nationally, while GPL barely moves at all.
executive_summary: Today, September 24, Emilia-Romagna's self-service prices stand at €2.1651/L for Benzina, €2.3593/L for Gasolio, €0.7580/L for GPL, and €1.8175/L for Metano, with 1,724 of the region's 1,882 registered stations reporting. Day-over-day moves were small: Benzina eased €0.0005 and Gasolio eased €0.0017 from September 22, while GPL and Metano held exactly flat — a quiet day at the pump on the surface.

But the ten-week weekly series tells a sharper story. Every fuel in Emilia-Romagna has risen since the tracking window opened in the week of July 20, but not at the same pace: Metano has surged 23.0%, nearly four points ahead of Italy's 19.1% national rise — the widest region-vs-nation gap in the dataset. Gasolio and Benzina have both climbed roughly 9%, tracking the national trend almost exactly, while GPL is the one fuel that has essentially stood still, down just 0.1% regionally versus a national dip of 0.5% — Emilia-Romagna's cheapest fuel is also its steadiest.

fuel_sections.heading: Benzina Holds Almost Exactly to the National Line
paragraphs: Today Emilia-Romagna's self-service Benzina averages €2.1651/L, essentially flat from September 22's €2.1656 — a move of just €0.0005. That puts it within three-tenths of a cent of Italy's national self-service average of €2.1654, one of the closest region-to-nation matches of any fuel today.

Zooming out to the weekly series, Emilia-Romagna's Benzina has climbed from €1.9736 in the week of July 20 (2026-W30) to €2.1651 in the week of September 21 (2026-W39, still building) — a rise of 9.7% over ten weeks. Nationally the increase over the same span was 9.6% (€1.9756 to €2.1655). The two lines have tracked each other closely throughout the period, making Benzina the fuel most in sync with the national trend this cycle.

fuel_sections.heading: Diesel Cools Slightly Today After a Sharp September Climb
paragraphs: Gasolio (diesel) self-service in Emilia-Romagna sits at €2.3593/L today, down €0.0017 from September 22's €2.3610 — a marginal pullback. That's now €0.0049 below the national self-service average of €2.3642, a gap that has only opened up in the past few days.

The multi-week story is steeper: Gasolio in Emilia-Romagna rose from €2.1695 (week of July 20) to €2.3591 (week of September 21), up 8.7% over ten weeks — almost identical to the national 8.7% rise (€2.1747 to €2.3631). What stands out is the shape of the climb: both region and nation were flat to easing through late July and early August (the region dipped to €2.1075 in the week of August 10), then accelerated sharply from the week of August 31 onward, with the region alone adding nearly €0.20 in the three weeks from August 31 to September 21.

fuel_sections.heading: GPL Is the One Fuel Standing Still
paragraphs: GPL self-service in Emilia-Romagna is unchanged today at €0.7580/L versus September 22, holding steady while the other three fuels moved. That price sits €0.0023 above the national self-service average of €0.7557 today.

GPL is the clear outlier of the four fuels over the ten-week tracked window: Emilia-Romagna's price has moved from €0.7599 (week of July 20) to €0.7588 (week of September 21), a decline of just 0.1%. Nationally the drop was larger, 0.5% (€0.7592 to €0.7557) — meaning the region's GPL price has held firmer than the national trend even as it remains by far the cheapest fuel at the pump, running at roughly a third of the Benzina price.

fuel_sections.heading: Metano Is Today's Real Story — and It's Been Building for Weeks
paragraphs: Metano is the standout: Emilia-Romagna's self-service price is €1.8175/L, unchanged from September 22, but that price now sits €0.0254 — 1.4% — above the national self-service average of €1.7921, the widest region-to-nation gap of any fuel tracked today.

The real story is the ten-week trend: Metano in Emilia-Romagna has surged from €1.4763 (week of July 20) to €1.8164 (week of September 21), a 23.0% increase — well ahead of the national 19.1% rise (€1.4999 to €1.7866) over the same span. That roughly four-point gap is the largest region-vs-nation divergence of any fuel in this entire dataset, and most of it opened up recently: the region added about €0.124 between the weeks of September 7 and September 21 alone, versus roughly €0.085 nationally over the same stretch — a noticeably faster climb than the rest of the country.

network_section.heading: Nearly 1,900 Stations, Nine in Ten Reporting Daily
paragraphs: Emilia-Romagna currently has 1,882 registered fuel stations, up from 1,876 when this tracking window opened on July 21 — a modest but steady net addition over the summer. Of those, 1,724 reported prices for September 24, a reporting rate of 91.6%.

That reporting rate runs slightly ahead of the national average of 90.3% (21,669 of 23,998 registered stations reporting nationwide on the same day), meaning Emilia-Romagna's network is marginally more consistent about daily price disclosure than Italy as a whole — useful context when reading the region's averages, since a broader, steadier reporting base makes today's figures more representative than in regions where participation swings more from day to day.

methodology_section.heading: How This Report Gets Made
paragraphs: Every figure in this report — the daily and weekly price series, the region-of-the-day selection, the region-vs-nation comparisons — comes from an unattended pipeline that pulls the Ministry of Enterprises' (MIMIT) official daily price and station-registry feeds, processes them, and rotates through Italy's 20 regions on a deterministic, date-keyed schedule so every region gets its turn. The prose itself, including this paragraph, is drafted automatically each morning by Claude Code reading that day's numbers directly out of the underlying data file.

That's a different model from a manually maintained spreadsheet, where someone has to remember to download the CSVs, paste them in, recompute the averages, and write up what changed. Here the whole chain — ingest, compute, write, publish, and even today's social post — runs without a human touching a keyboard, which is also why the analysis stays grounded strictly in the numbers on file rather than editorializing beyond what the data supports.

caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight: Emilia-Romagna, where pump prices are telling a more interesting story than they first appear.

Diesel and petrol both crept down slightly day-over-day, but zoom out to the ten-week trend and one fuel stands out: Metano (natural gas) is up 23% in Emilia-Romagna since late July, outpacing Italy's national average by roughly four percentage points — the biggest region-vs-nation gap of any fuel we're tracking right now.

Fuel Dashboard is a live, self-updating interactive dashboard covering all 20 Italian regions, every province, municipality, and major fuel brand — rebuilt every morning from the Ministry of Enterprises' official price and station data. No one is opening a spreadsheet to paste in yesterday's CSV: an automated pipeline built with Claude Code pulls the data, computes the trends, drafts today's regional report, and publishes it — including this post — without a human in the loop. That's the case for building with AI tools instead of maintaining a manual Excel sheet: what used to be a chore someone has to remember to do every morning is now a system that just runs.
